newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares close more than three percent higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares close more than three percent higher.

text.p: Swiss shares closed more than three percent higher on a favourable reaction to U.S Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before congress, a stronger dollar and positive company results, dealers said.
The banking sector also benefitted from continued optimism following the merger of two Munich-based banks.
Pharmaceuticals also benefitted from good Clariant results, dealers said.
* The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) was up 3.4 percent, or 192.8 points, to 5,869.9.
* The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 2.84 percent, or 102.31 points, to 3,708.
Clariant, which announced a 24 percent rise in first half sales this morning, rose 45 francs to 1050. Ciba profited from Clariant's good result and jumped 7.5 francs to 141.
Novartis, whose sales figures for the first half are expected on Thursday, rose more than five percent to 2.446 francs.
The market expects good to very good figures.
Financials, which were under pressure a few days ago, profited from the merger-announcement of two German banks.
"The strong rise of bank-shares in Germany, also triggered Swiss shares", one dealer said.
Shares of UBS rose 44 francs to 1,698, Credit Suisse advanced around six percent or 12.25 francs to 204.75 and SBC registered shares jumped 15.5 francs to 421.

Rentenanstalt/Swiss Life soared 52 francs or more than seven percent to 728 and SAirGroup advanced 53 francs to 1,881. BB Medtech rose 7.74 percent to 1,810 francs after announcing good company results on Tuesday.
On the Swiss Option and Financial Future Exchange (Soffex) trade in SMI-Futures was hectic, dealers said.
The August SMI rose 203 points to 5,878. One dealer said, a lot of people might have taken short positions today. This might weaken potential support on Thursday, he added.
In all, 102,093 options changed hands. The call/put ratio was 2.52 to one.
